raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Models served through the Transformers fallback fail to load when the checkpoint ships tensors that the HF model never constructs. For example, `LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.5-33B` (`Exaone4_5_ForConditionalGeneration`) has no native SGLang implementation, and its checkpoint includes an MTP head (`mtp.*`) that is not used for serving:

```
ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.mtp' in TransformersMultiModalForCausalLM.
```

HF declares such keys on the model class (`Exaone4_5_PreTrainedModel._keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected = [r"mtp.*"]`) and drops them in `_adjust_missing_and_unexpected_keys`. The fallback loader has no equivalent, so it raises on them.

## Modifications

- `AutoWeightsLoader` gets an `ignore_unexpected_patterns` argument (regexes, matched with `re.search` like HF). It sits next to the existing `ignore_unexpected_prefixes` / `ignore_unexpected_suffixes`.
- `TransformersBase.load_weights` passes `self.model._keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected`. This is the HF model's own list; `post_init` aggregates it from submodules.

The patterns apply only on the "no module or parameter" path (`_can_ignore_unexpected`). This matches HF, which filters only keys that are already unexpected. Some HF patterns also name real layers, so this ordering matters. GLM-4-MoE uses `[r"model\.layers\.92.*", r"model\.layers\.46.*"]`, one for the MTP layer of each model size. Applied as a pre-filter, these patterns would drop the real layer 46 of the 92-layer model. Here that parameter still loads.

Models that don't set the attribute get an empty set or `None`, so their behavior is unchanged. A checkpoint key that matches no module, parameter or pattern still raises.

## Accuracy Tests

`LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.5-33B` on Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60 x4), transformers backend:

```
SGLANG_USE_SGL_XPU=1 sglang serve --model-path LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.5-33B --device xpu --tp-size 4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 --trust-remote-code --attention-backend intel_xpu
```

(`--max-prefill-tokens 4096` is an XPU memory-headroom setting, unrelated to this change.)

On main the server fails at weight load with the error above. With this PR it loads (17.55 GB per GPU, 24192 KV-cache tokens) and answers image prompts correctly (it reads "XPU 42" from a rendered text image).

gsm8k, all 1319 questions, 5-shot, chat template, 16 concurrent:

| Filter | exact_match |
| --- | --- |
| flexible-extract | 0.2092 ± 0.0112 |
| strict-match | 0.0182 ± 0.0037 |

All 1319 requests completed without errors. The score is low because EXAONE-4.5 is a reasoning model: lm_eval's default 256-token generation limit for gsm8k cuts the `<think>` block off before the final answer. A native SGLang implementation of the model (local, not upstreamed) scored the same with the same eval command (flexible-extract 0.1986), so the low score does not come from the fallback.

Unit tests: `test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_transformers_fallback.py` (CPU suite) gets 2 new cases:
- a pattern that matches a real parameter still loads that parameter, while a key with no parameter is dropped;
- a key that matches no pattern still raises.

All cases in the file pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. This only changes the weight-loading path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body:
CUDA check on 1x NVIDIA H200 NVL (tp 1). Both runs use the same image (`lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261015-a6a8c560`) with the sglang Python source taken from each commit:
- before: merge-base `91f6ef2322`
- after: this PR `be6dac5bb0`

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Before | fails at weight load: `ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.mtp' in TransformersMultiModalForCausalLM.` |
| After | loads and serves; gsm8k (all 1319, 5-shot, chat template) strict-match 0.0152, flexible-extract 0.2032 |

The CUDA gsm8k numbers are in line with the XPU run in the description (0.0182 / 0.2092).

```bash
sglang serve --model-path LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.5-33B --tp-size 1 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --trust-remote-code

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args pretrained=LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.5-33B,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=16 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 16 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --seed 42
```

Reviewing this patch as part of the weekly XPU consolidation (#45201), I found two reproducible gaps in the HF ignore-pattern handling:

1. **Full-key patterns are checked against truncated module prefixes.** In `AutoWeightsLoader._load_module`, an unexpected `layers.1.weight` is checked as `layers.1` or `layers.1.`. With `ignore_unexpected_patterns=[r"layers\.1\.weight$"]`, the regex matches the complete checkpoint key, but loading still raises `ValueError: No module or parameter named 'layers.1'`. The added `layers\.2.*` regression does not catch this because it also matches the truncated prefix. Please evaluate complete unexpected weight names while retaining the rule that existing parameters must still load.

2. **The fallback mapper changes names before unchanged HF patterns are evaluated.** Using `TransformersBase.hf_to_sglang_mapper`, checkpoint key `mtp.weight` becomes `model.mtp.weight`. An HF pattern such as `r"^mtp.*"` matches the original key but not the mapped name, and the loader raises `ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.mtp'`. Several Transformers models use this pattern. Please preserve the relationship between original checkpoint names, mapped names, and ignore patterns without filtering real parameters that match.

I reproduced both cases on CPU using the production loader and mapper. The current `test_transformers_fallback.py` suite passes (3 tests), so please add regressions for both cases, alongside the existing real-parameter preservation and unmatched-key checks. These content fixes should be addressed in this source PR before it is carried into a merge-ready consolidation.

@@ -1098,6 +1098,8 @@ def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
             skip_substrs=self.skip_substrs,

             ignore_unexpected_suffixes=self.ignore_unexpected_suffixes,
+            # Checkpoint keys HF itself drops on load, e.g. an MTP head unused for serving.
+            ignore_unexpected_patterns=self.model._keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected,
         )

@@ -14,6 +14,7 @@

 import itertools

 from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
 from functools import lru_cache
@@ -141,6 +142,7 @@ def __init__(
         skip_substrs: list[str] | None = None,
         ignore_unexpected_prefixes: list[str] | None = None,
         ignore_unexpected_suffixes: list[str] | None = None,
+        ignore_unexpected_patterns: Iterable[str] | None = None,
     ) -> None:
         self.module = module
         self.skip_prefixes = list(skip_prefixes or [])
@@ -150,6 +152,9 @@ def __init__(
         ]
         self.ignore_unexpected_prefixes = list(ignore_unexpected_prefixes or [])
         self.ignore_unexpected_suffixes = list(ignore_unexpected_suffixes or [])
+        self.ignore_unexpected_patterns = [
+            re.compile(p) for p in ignore_unexpected_patterns or ()
+        ]
 
     def _groupby_prefix(
         self,
@@ -182,9 +187,11 @@ def _can_skip(self, qualname: str) -> bool:
         )
 
     def _can_ignore_unexpected(self, qualname: str) -> bool:
-        return any(
-            qualname.startswith(p) for p in self.ignore_unexpected_prefixes
-        ) or any(qualname.endswith(s) for s in self.ignore_unexpected_suffixes)
+        return (
+            any(qualname.startswith(p) for p in self.ignore_unexpected_prefixes)
+            or any(qualname.endswith(s) for s in self.ignore_unexpected_suffixes)
+            or any(p.search(qualname) for p in self.ignore_unexpected_patterns)
+        )
 
     def _load_param(
         self,

@@ -2,7 +2,10 @@
 
 import unittest
 
+import torch
+
 from sglang.srt.models.transformers import TransformersBase
+from sglang.srt.models.utils import AutoWeightsLoader
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
 from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
 
@@ -37,5 +40,40 @@ def test_gpt_neox_prefix_rewrites(self):
         )
 
 
+class TestAutoWeightsLoaderIgnoreUnexpectedPatterns(CustomTestCase):
+    def _make_loader(self) -> tuple[torch.nn.Module, AutoWeightsLoader]:
+        module = torch.nn.Module()
+        module.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList(
+            [torch.nn.Linear(2, 2, bias=False) for _ in range(2)]
+        )
+        # GLM-4-MoE style: one pattern names an MTP-only layer, the other a real layer.
+        loader = AutoWeightsLoader(
+            module, ignore_unexpected_patterns=[r"layers\.2.*", r"layers\.1.*"]
+        )
+        return module, loader
+
+    def test_skips_only_keys_without_a_parameter(self):
+        # HF `_keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected` regexes must drop checkpoint keys
+        # with no matching parameter, but still load a real parameter they match.
+        module, loader = self._make_loader()
+
+        loaded = loader.load_weights(
+            [
+                ("layers.0.weight", torch.ones(2, 2)),
+                ("layers.1.weight", torch.full((2, 2), 2.0)),
+                ("layers.2.weight", torch.zeros(2, 2)),
+            ]
+        )
+
+        self.assertEqual(loaded, {"layers.0.weight", "layers.1.weight"})
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(module.layers[1].weight, torch.full((2, 2), 2.0)))
+
+    def test_unmatched_unexpected_key_still_raises(self):
+        _, loader = self._make_loader()
+
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "No module or parameter named"):
+            loader.load_weights([("mtp.weight", torch.zeros(2, 2))])
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
